title: Nearly quadratic-stretch pseudorandom generators for randomized Turing machines
author: Emanuele Viola
work: Pseudorandom Bits and Lower Bounds for Randomized Turing Machines
source_version: Theory of Computing18 (2022), Article10, publisher source publicationMay 20, 2022; DOI10.4086/toc.2022.v018a010

source_locator.proof_scope: Complete author argument including supplied core constructions

difficulty_reason: The generator’s correctness depends on a new blockwise simulation that validates a canonical minimum-crossing partition and accepts for exactly one guessed crossing sequence. That uniqueness permits summing branching-program approximation errors at exponentially small accuracy while retaining the stated nearly square-root seed length; the work goes beyond ordinary qualification-exam machine simulations.

source_check.note: Full article including randomized machine and branching-program models; Theorem2.2 uniquely accepting crossing-sequence simulation and its complete Section3 construction. Forbes–Kelley branching-program PRG is an external precisely cited prerequisite, not an omitted source-local argument. Theorem1.2 constructs a pseudorandom generator for two-tape RTMs, while Theorem1.4 gives a time lower bound for three-tape RTM2 computations. The latter has a separate new Section4 simulation and hierarchy contradiction, so it is not merely a complementary or parameter-restated formulation of the generator. Supporting simulation Theorem2.2 and both claims stay uncounted.
